title: ecc-burst-correlation-sprint-log
content:
Summary:
This is a sprint-style investigation log and runbook fragment for recurring short ECC bursts observed across a subset of our A100 fleet. Goal: capture raw on-call steps, correlators we tried, quick mitigations, and a minimal automated alerting threshold to reduce pager noise while surfacing real regressions.

Background and motivation:
- Since 2025-08-30 we've seen intermittent increases in correctable ECC counts on ~6-10% of nodes in a single rack during afternoon traffic peaks.
- Symptoms vary: some nodes show rising correctable counts without VM impact; others progress to driver requeue/Xid timeouts and occasional kernel oops on the gpu driver.
- Existing alerts are too noisy (alert on any non-zero CC count). We need a more actionable runbook and a short-term quarantine policy.

Event timeline (concise):
- 2025-09-02 14:12 UTC: First pager for node rgx-ct-19: correctable-ecc-rate spike reported by metric-rule (1-min window).
- 14:15: On-call (Asha) SSH into rgx-ct-19. Ran quick checks: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC; dmesg | grep -i nvrm; kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data rgx-ct-19 (evacuation).
- 14:22: Observed repeated ECC correctable counts in nvidia-smi (increments every ~30s). Temperature normal, GPU utilization low.
- 14:45: Driver reload attempted (modprobe -r nvidia_uvm; modprobe nvidia_uvm) — temporarily suppressed bursts for ~40m.
- 15:30: Correctable counts resumed; Xid 61 transient errors started in dmesg. Node cordoned and put in quarantine pool.
- 2025-09-03 10:00: Rebooted node with PSU power cycle (requested datacenter staff). After reboot counts remained elevated on next boot.
- 2025-09-05: Cross-check with hardware vendor (ticket created). Vendor suggested collecting ECC counters over time and checking nvlink/link-error counters.

Quick investigation notes and commands used:
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC  <-- per-gpu ECC counts (correctable, uncorrectable)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.corrected.volatile.total,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 5
- dmesg | egrep -i "Xid|NVRM|nvidia|gpu"
- smartctl -a /dev/sda (to rule out storage-related kernel interactions; usually negative)
- ethtool -S on host NICs to ensure PCIe RAS counters not spiking
- nvidia-smi nvlink --verbose (NVLink link error counters)
- pciutils: lspci -vvv | egrep -A4 "NVIDIA" to inspect AER reports
- ipmitool sdr list (to correlate PSU/board sensor events)

Observed correlations that look promising (hypotheses):
1) Burst windows align with short-duration power draw fluctuations in the rack (PSU sensor spikes). Not every node with PSUs flagged shows ECC bursts, but there is a temporal overlap in almost all incidents.
2) Driver reloads temporarily suppress the visible correctable-count growth, suggesting either a reporting/state drift in the GPU driver or transient firmware state that clears on module reload.
3) Nodes with dense NVLink topologies and >1 GPU per server show higher likelihood of progressing to Xid errors when ECC correctables accelerate.
4) Kernel upgrade in 2025-07 produced a small uptick in correctable reporting across the fleet, but not at the burst rate we see now. Could be a second-order interaction (kernel niceness + PSU ripple).

Runbook fragment: immediate actions (one-liners for on-call)
- Step 0: Triage quickly (5m): check host heat, nvidia-smi ECC delta, dmesg for Xid, and whether any pods were OOMKilled. Commands: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC; dmesg | tail -n 200 | egrep -i "Xid|NVRM"
- Step 1: If correctable rate > 5/min (observed over rolling 1m window across any single GPU), automatically: cordon + drain node with graceful timeout 10m, add to quarantine label: kubectl label node <node> gpu-quarantine=true --overwrite.
- Step 2: Capture diagnostics: save nvidia-smi output, dmesg, /var/log/messages; run nvlink counters. Archive to s3: s3://redwood-gpu-diagnostics/<node>/<timestamp>/
- Step 3: Try a driver module reload (low-risk): modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia && modprobe nvidia nvidia_drm nvidia_uvm; monitor for 15m. If counts drop and stay flat for 30m, uncordon after validation.
- Step 4: If driver reload fails or Xid errors persist, escalate to hardware triage and vendor support; do not power-cycle without vendor guidance if node under warranty.
- Step 5: If repeated within 24h after reload and vendor advises, schedule PSU swap + full power cycle with datacenter tech.

Why 5/min?
- We calibrated thresholds on a subset of historical events: background noise is typically <1/min. 5/min in 1m rolling window corresponds to a sustained burst that historically preceded more severe driver errors in ~60% of observed cases. This reduces noise from soft transient ECC increments.

Automation proposals (near-term):
- Implement a Prometheus alert rule: rate(nvidia_ecc_correctable_total[1m]) > 5 for any gpu -> route to SRE queue with runbook link.
- Add automated collection job that, when triggered, snapshots ECC counters every 10s for 10m and uploads to diagnostics bucket (to capture burst shape).
- Add a k8s node-label-based routing policy to prevent scheduling of latency-sensitive workloads into the quarantine pool.

Longer-term experiments to run in a controlled test rack:
- Controlled PSU ripple injection (with datacenter) to test ECC increase reproducibility.
- Booting into older driver kernel combos to see change in ECC-reporting cadence.
- Swap NVLink groups (re-cable in vendor-supported config) to confirm topology sensitivity.
- Run a stress test (cuda-memtest or custom kernel) to see whether induced bitflips are correctable or persistent.

Notes to self / open questions:
- We still need to determine whether driver reload actually resets GPU-internal scrubbing state or just driver counters. Need firmware-level counters from vendor.
- Should we instrument pcie AER counters centrally? (yes, add to infra backlog).
- Is there a correlation with specific datacenter racks / BMC firmware versions? Quick sample shows two incidents in rack r24 that share BMC rev 1.2.9.
- What is the expected behavior of ECC scrubbing on our HW under sustained load? (ask hardware team for spec).

Post-incident follow-ups (action items):
- SRE: implement Prometheus rule + collection job (owner: Riley Chen, due: 2025-09-26)
- HW liaison: request firmware ECC dump capability from vendor and ask whether driver reload clears scrub state (owner: Diego Morales, due: 2025-09-20)
- Infra: add node label / scheduling policy for quarantine pool (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2025-09-30)
- Run a controlled PSU ripple experiment (coordinated with datacenter) (owner: Asha Menon, tentative window: 2025-10-10)

Appendix: quick snippet examples collected during a burst:
- nvidia-smi excerpt:
GPU 0: Correctable ECC: 245 -> 258 (observed 13 in 5m)
GPU 1: Correctable ECC: 180 -> 204 (observed 24 in 5m)
- dmesg excerpt:
[12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 61, PID: 0, GPU:0, Faulted channel: 0
[12346.001210] nvidia: GPU 0000:3b:00: GPU has incurred a fatal error and cannot continue

Useful links and references (internal):
- Slack thread: #sre-gpu-ops, thread id 78910
- Vendor ticket: NVND-2025-3345
- Related infra PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/421

Final notes: This doc is a working log. Convert to an official runbook after we validate alert thresholds and collect a week of automated snapshots. Keep conservative quarantine (cordon+drain) as default until we have firmware confirmation that driver reload is safe and reliable for clearing transient hardware state.

Unresolved: whether to automatically reboot after two reload failures — leaving as manual for now to avoid warranty/power-cycle surprises.

-- Asha
